principle: Mathematical proposition content, proof objects, source artifacts and proof status are distinct records.

proposition_status_model.policy: Status is relative to mathematical scope and review state; it is not a node type or generic confidence score.

proof_record.policy: A Proof record is a derivation object. A source can contain or describe it without being identical to it.

relation_candidates.definition: A specified source or formal framework defines a term using specified mathematical content.
A proof is assessed as establishing a proposition relative to its assumptions/framework.
A proof uses a proposition, definition, lemma or prior result as an explicit dependency.
A formal artifact encodes a proposition or definition in a named formal system/library.
Records mathematical proof status without turning status into a primitive edge.

guardrails: No theorem/conjecture node type is required merely because a proposition is proved or open.
No proof status is inferred from popularity, citation count, numerical testing or model confidence.
A formal-system theorem declaration is not counted as an independent historical proof unless its derivation/provenance is separately modeled.
No equivalence between Euclidean and modern prime definitions is asserted by default.
Counterexamples and implications must match proposition scope and assumptions.
